name: Sikalastic-701

SIKALASTIC®-701: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikalastic®-701, April 2023, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/e/sikalastic-701.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikalastic®-701 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description.
    - Sikalastic®-701 is a 2-part, polyurethane hybrid, gloss finish top coat for Sika® Liquid Applied Membrane waterproofing systems.
    - Sikalastic®-701 is commonly used in conjunction with SikaRoof® MTC-UV systems and can also be used with Sikalastic® polyurea systems.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikalastic®-701 may only be used by experienced professionals.
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - A gloss finish top coat for.
    - Sika® Liquid Applied Membrane systems
    - Sika® 2-C spray applied PU/PUA systems
    - Newly applied or renovating existing membranes
    - Flat and pitched roof structures
    - Communal walkways
    - Podium decks
    - Terrace roofs
    - For exterior use only
    For the following waterproofing system applications:
1.5 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikalastic®-701
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Polyurethane hybrid elastic top coat for liquid applied membrane waterproofing systems
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to European Technical Assessment ETA-20/0248, based on ETAG 005 Part 1 and Part 6 — Liquid applied roof waterproofing kits. Part 1: General. Part 6: Specific stipulations for Kits based on Polyurethane
    - Fire Testing EN 13501-1, Sikalastic®-701, Sikalastic®- 702, warringtonfire, Report No.19896B
    - Abrasion resistance AR0.5(Special), Sikalastic®-701, Sikalastic®-702, FACE, Test report No. FC/18/8048
    - AS4654.1:2012 Waterproofing membranes for external above-ground use (BRANZ)
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ETA-20/0248: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - ETAG 005: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 13501-1: cited with a stated property or value; listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1); Technical Information > Reaction to fire (p.2).
    - AS4654.1:2012: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN ISO 2811-11: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - EN ISO 527-3: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strain at break (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - ASTM C1549: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Solar reflectance (p.2).
    - ASTM C1371: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Thermal emittance (p.2).
    - EN 29117:1992: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Tack free time (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Aliphatic polyurethane providing UV and yellowing resistance
    - Good long term weathering performance
    - Good colour stability and gloss retention
    - Good chemical resistance
    - Low soiling and easily cleanable
    - Suitable for cool roofs by providing a high Solar Reflective Index
    - Resistant to ponding water
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Elastomeric Polyurethane/Hybrid
    - Colour: Light Grey (RAL 7035); White (RAL 9016)
    - Density: ~1.25 kg/l (mixed A+B); Value at +23 °C (DIN EN ISO 2811-11)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Chemical resistance: Resistant to many chemicals. Contact Sika Technical Service for additional information.
2.7 Solid content by mass.
    | Part A | ~67 % |
    | Part B | ~100 % |
2.8 Solid content by volume.
    | Part A | ~55 % |
    | Part B | ~100 % |
2.9 Tensile strength.
    | Temperature | Value |
    | +23 °C | ~10 MPa |
    | -20 °C | ~20 MPa |
    Test method printed: (EN ISO 527-3)
2.10 Tensile strain at break.
    | Temperature | Value |
    | +23 °C | ~100 % |
    | -20 °C | ~20 % |
    Test method printed: (EN ISO 527-3)
2.11 Solar reflectance.
    | Initial Solar Reflectance | 0,88 |
    Test method printed: (ASTM C1549)
2.12 Thermal emittance.
    | Initial Thermal Emittance | 0,86 |
    Test method printed: (ASTM C1371)
2.13 Solar reflectance index.
    | Initial SRI (Convective Coefficient, | ~112 |
    | Medium Wind) |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.14 External fire performance.
    | Broof T1 / Broof T4 | (prEN 1187) |
2.15 Reaction to fire.
    | Euroclass E | (EN 13501-1) |
2.16 System structure. Sikalastic®-701 can be used with the following: 1-Part PU cold applied Systems
    - Sikalastic®-488/SL
    - Sikalastic®-888
    - Sikalastic®-851 R
    - Sikalastic®-888
    - Sikalastic®-888 Hybrid
    - SikaRoof® MTC- UV
    2-Part PU/PUA hot spray applied Systems
    Refer to the following System Data Sheets:
2.17 Dry film thickness. Dry film thickness (DFT): 220 micron
2.18 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store properly in original, unopened and undamaged packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Always refer to packaging.
2.19 Packaging.
    | Part A | 10kg container |
    | Part B | 2.5kg container |
    | Part A + B | 12.5kg ready to mix unit |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - Confirm waiting /overcoating time has been achieved on the previously applied system base layer. The base layer must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and loose material. If dust exists on the surface, it must be completely removed before application of the product, preferably by vacuum extraction equipment.
    - If the maximum overcoating time of the base layer is exceeded, the surface must be lightly abraded using light abrasive manual tools or mechanical equipment to roughen the surface. Depending on the type of base layer, a solvent wipe may also be required. Finally, completely remove all the dust by vacuum extraction equipment.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : Part B = 80 : 20 (by volume)
    - Consumption: Wet film thickness (WFT): 280 micron; Approximately 35m2 per 12.5kg pail
    - Yield: ~0.35 kg/m² applied in a single coat
    - Pot Life: 1 hour at +20 °C; Pot life will decrease at higher temperatures and increase at lower temperatures.
4.3 Tack free time.
    | Condition | Property | Value |
    | 20 °C / 50 % RH | Tack free time | ~45 minutes |
    | 20 °C / 50 % RH | Hard drying time | ~60 minutes |
    | 20 °C / 50 % RH | Final drying time | ~90 minutes |
    | Condition | Property | Value |
    | 5  °C / 50 % RH | Tack free time | ~75 minutes |
    | 5 °C / 50 % RH | Hard drying time | ~105 minutes |
    | 5 °C / 50 % RH | Final drying time | ~135 minutes |
    Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity.
    Test method printed: (EN 29117:1992)
    Test method printed: (EN 29117:1992)
4.4 Applied product ready for use.
    | Temperature | Relative Hu- | Rain Resist- | Foot Traffic | Full Cure |
    | midity | ant |
    | +10 °C | 50 % | ~75 minutes | ~150 minutes | ~1 day |
    | +20 °C | 50 % | ~60 minutes | ~120 minutes | ~1 day |
    | +30 °C | 50 % | ~45 minutes | ~90 minutes | ~16 hours |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity.
4.5 Mixing. Prior to mixing all parts, mix separately Part A (resin) using an electric single or double paddle mixer and stirrer (300 to 400 rpm) or other suitable equipment. Mix liquid and all the coloured pigment until a uniform colour / mix has been achieved. Add Part B (hardener) to Part A and mix Part A + B continuously for 3,0 minutes until a uniformly coloured mix has been achieved. Mix full units only. Mixing time for A+B = ~3,0 minutes.
4.6 Application. Apply mixed product in 1 coat by roller, brush or spray equipment to achieve a consistent thickness and required surface finish.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened material can only be removed mechanically or with a proprietary paint stripper.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations. Installation work must only be carried out by Sika® trained and approved contractors, experienced in this type of application.
    - Products must only be applied in accordance with their intended use.
    - Do not use for indoor applications.
    - Do not apply near to running air intakes of air conditioning units. Switch off units before applying.
    - Do not dilute with any solvent or water.
4.9 Further information.
    - Safety Data Sheet (SDS)
    - Sika Method Statement: SikaRoof® MTC-UV systems

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +2 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity.
    | Above +20 °C | 35 % min / 80 % max. |
    | Below +20 °C | 45 % min. / 80 % max. |
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation. The substrate and uncured applied membrane must be at least +3 °C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the membrane finish.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +2 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. Refer to Product Data Sheet of the appropriate base layers
5.7 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: ~1.25 kg/l (mixed A+B); Value at +23 °C (DIN EN ISO 2811-11)
    - Tensile strength: Temperature | Value; +23 °C | ~10 MPa; -20 °C | ~20 MPa (EN ISO 527-3)
    - Tensile strain at break: Temperature | Value; +23 °C | ~100 %; -20 °C | ~20 % (EN ISO 527-3)
    - Solar reflectance: Initial Solar Reflectance | 0,88 (ASTM C1549)
    - Thermal emittance: Initial Thermal Emittance | 0,86 (ASTM C1371)
    - Tack free time: Condition | Property | Value; 20 °C / 50 % RH | Tack free time | ~45 minutes; 20 °C / 50 % RH | Hard drying time | ~60 minutes; 20 °C / 50 % RH | Final drying time | ~90 minutes; Condition | Property | Value; 5  °C / 50 % RH | Tack free time | ~75 minutes; 5 °C / 50 % RH | Hard drying time | ~105 minutes; 5 °C / 50 % RH | Final drying time | ~135 minutes; Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity. (EN 29117:1992) (EN 29117:1992)
5.8 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.9 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikalastic®-701, April 2023, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/e/sikalastic-701.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikalastic®-701 Part A, version 06/05/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/y/sds-sikalastic-701parta.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikalastic 701 Part B, version 18/04/2023, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/m/Sikalastic%20701%20Part%20B%20GHS7%20.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
